title: Registry.validatePayload never validates against the registered JSON Schema -- ES-05 schema enforcement is a no-op
notes:
Discovered while resolving ISS-0148 (GH #464). TC-ES-05-02 ('append with payload failing registered schema returns PayloadSchemaInvalid') could not be made a real test at EITHER unit or integration level, because the behaviour it asserts does not exist in production code.

src/event_store/registry.zig Registry.validatePayload fetches the registered EventTypeRecord, immediately discards it (`_ = record;`), then performs only a structural is-JSON-object check and returns. It carries an explicit TODO: 'full JSON Schema draft-07 validation against record.json_schema when a JSON Schema validator is available.'

Consequence: ES-05's core acceptance criterion -- 'WHEN a caller appends a payload that fails the registered schema, THEN the platform returns HTTP 422 with an RFC 9457 body listing every validation failure (field path, constraint violated, actual value)' -- is unenforced. Any JSON object payload is accepted for any registered event type regardless of its schema. The ValidationFailure struct and lastValidationFailures() accessor exist but are only ever populated with a single synthetic '/' + 'type' entry for non-object payloads.

This is a production gap, not a test gap. ES-05 is currently marked RELEASED in docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, which overstates its true state.
candidate_resolution: Implement JSON Schema draft-07 validation in Registry.validatePayload against record.json_schema, populating last_failures with one ValidationFailure per violated constraint (field_path as RFC 6901 pointer, constraint keyword, serialised actual value). Then add TC-ES-05-02 as an integration test and re-derive ES-05's status. Note getType() also returns a placeholder record with json_schema hardcoded to '{}' rather than parsing the queried row -- that must be fixed first or schema validation will have nothing real to validate against.
